az_powerline_crag.blurb: Powerline Crag is a small limestone sport wall in the forest of northern Arizona, filed with the Winslow area crags along the Highway 87 and 99 corridors. It holds 19 bolted lines, all short, and the grades spread from 5.7 up to a single 5.12, with the bulk of the routes in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. The setting is wooded, so expect pine shade around the base rather than an open desert face. The routes are brief single pitches, which makes it a handy stop for a quick session or a warm-up day rather than a destination for long climbing days.

az_bastion_towers.blurb: Bastion Towers is a cluster of half a dozen granite formations at the south end of the Rockfellow Group in the East Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, southeast Arizona. The ground between the towers is a tangle of fissures and chimneys, and the stone wears bright lichen. Climbing here is mostly traditional, with a pair of bolted lines, and routes run one to three pitches. Difficulty covers a wide range, from moderate 5.8 and 5.9 cracks to a handful at 5.12. Route-finding and a real walk-in are part of the day, so this suits parties comfortable on multi-pitch trad in a remote, backcountry setting.

az_foreplay_wall.blurb: Foreplay Wall is a compact granite crag in Stewart Pocket, a short drive from Payson in central Arizona. It is the closest wall to the trailhead, set on the slope directly above the car park, so the walk is brief. Eighteen routes mix trad, sport and a few top-rope options. Grades start at 5.6 and climb through the 5.10s, with a couple of lines at 5.11 and 5.12, so there is something for beginners and a few harder tests. The wall catches sun early and goes into shade by the afternoon, which makes it a comfortable pick for warmer days.

az_movie_quote_wall_the.blurb: The Movie Quote Wall is a west-facing limestone sport wall in the Homestead canyon of central Arizona. It has 18 bolted routes, mostly long single pitches around 60 to 80 feet. The core of the wall is 5.10 to 5.11, with a couple of easier lines at 5.8 and 5.9 to get started. Many climbs pull over a small roof that is often not the hardest part. The wall is shady in the morning and picks up sun in mid-afternoon. It is a gentler introduction to the Homestead than some of its steeper, more technical walls. Be mindful of climbers on the routes below.

az_murray_wall_the.blurb: The Murray Wall is a small granite sport wall among the Summit Crags high on Mount Lemmon, north of Tucson, at roughly 8,500 feet. Eighteen routes, nearly all bolted, run from 5.7 up to 5.12, with the main face concentrated in the 5.11 range and a few easier lines at its side. The cooler elevation and long periods of shade make it a summer refuge when the desert floor is too hot. Foot traffic is light since most walkers head on to other walls. It is often used as a warm-up before the steeper nearby face, and top-roping is possible from above.

az_south_wall_2.blurb: South Wall is a long, rounded boulder in the Tinkerbell Wall zone of Euro Dog Valley, part of the Oak Flat bouldering near Queen Creek Canyon in central Arizona. It faces north, so it stays comfortable on warmer days. Eighteen problems are packed along it, mostly shorter than those on the neighbouring north side. Grades run from V0 warm-ups through V2 to V4, with a cluster of V3 and V4 problems and one standout hard line near V7. Expect a quiet wash setting where water may sit nearby after wet weather.
